summary: Partitioned SIEM export with hourly checksums, UTC canonicalization, and GDPR deletion proof requested
description:
Issue summary:
Customer requests a partitioned SIEM export format for EU region with: hourly partitions, per-file SHA256 checksums, canonicalized timestamps normalized to UTC (with original offset preserved in metadata), KMS-wrapped signed manifest, and explicit proof of deletion for GDPR DSARs. They report mismatch between timestamps in console and exported objects which complicates deduplication during ingest into their SIEM.

Impact:
FinLeaf ingestion pipeline is failing to reconcile events for March 28 DST boundary; this prevents timely fraud detection and delays compliance evidence delivery. They have an upcoming audit and require signed proof that redacted/deleted user events were removed from exported archives.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted (prod)
- Region: eu-west
- Customer export job: siem-export-job-2026-03-eu
- Destination: customer S3 bucket (s3://finleaf-logs/redwood-eu/)
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In Console, schedule a SIEM export for time range 2026-03-28T00:00:00+01:00 to 2026-03-29T00:00:00+01:00 using 'hourly-partition' template
2) Wait for export job completion notification and download three artifacts: data-*.ndjson.gz, manifest.json.sig, checksums.sha256
3) Inspect timestamps in events (event.time) and the object name timestamps (partition keys) and compare to console's time-range display
4) Run FinLeaf ingestion validation script which rejects events with event.time outside partition range due to apparent DST offset mismatch
expected_behavior:
- Exported event timestamps are canonicalized to UTC in the payload and original timezone offset is preserved in event.metadata.original_offset.
- Object partition keys and checksums align with UTC-normalized timestamps so downstream deduplication works.
- Manifest is KMS-wrapped and signed; manifest contains signed per-file SHA256 and a signed deletion-proof block for any purged IDs during retention window.
actual_behavior:
- Several events in exported files show event.time values that, when converted to UTC, appear shifted by +/-1 hour relative to the object partition key leading to rejection by FinLeaf pipeline.
- Manifest includes checksums but does not include a signed deletion proof block.
- Checksums file uses newline-delimited '<sha256> <filename>' but the ordering is inconsistent across retries and has caused non-deterministic verification failures.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 09:45 UTC: Support confirmed existence of export artifacts and collected attached files from customer.

2026-03-12 11:10 UTC: SRE reproduced timestamp discrepancy in staging using DST boundary fixture. Hypothesis: exporter uses local region timestamp for partition key but writes event.time as application-level timestamp without normalization during archive write path.
2026-03-12 14:00 UTC: Eng traced checksums generation to retry path where ordering isn't stable; small race leads to deterministic but non-reproducible ordering across job retries.
2026-03-12 16:30 UTC: Confirmed manifest format does not include deletion-proof block currently; design exists in runbook but not implemented in exporter v1.
comments: 2026-03-12 10:05 - Aisha Patel (Support): Received customer's request and attachments. Assigning to SRE for initial triage. SLA due by 2026-03-13.

2026-03-12 11:20 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Reproduced locally using DST fixture. I see partition key generator uses zone-aware localtime; will add unit tests. Asking Eng to review checksums ordering logic. (linked: github.com/redwood-inference/audit-exporter/issues/210)

2026-03-12 15:05 - Elena Kim (Engineering): Confirmed bug in exporter v1. Working on two PRs: one to canonicalize event.time to UTC payload and preserve original offset in metadata, and one to produce deterministic checksum ordering (sort by filename). ETA for PRs: 1 business day.

2026-03-12 18:40 - FinLeaf Technical Contact (customer): We need signed deletion proof for IDs removed last month for an auditor. Can you include a signed manifest block that enumerates deleted event IDs and signing timestamp?

2026-03-13 08:30 - Aisha Patel (Support): Noted customer ask. Confirmed runbook for deletion-proof exists; Eng to add signed block signed with KMS key redwood-exporter-signing-key and include a revocation proof chain.
action_items: Eng-1: Implement UTC canonicalization and original_offset preservation in exporter (PR #482).
Eng-2: Make checksums generation deterministic by sorting filenames before hash file creation (PR #483).
Eng-3: Extend manifest schema to include signed deletion_proof array and integrate KMS signing (ticket: ENG-exports-527).
SRE-1: Run a migration job to regenerate March 28 export for FinLeaf using exporter v2 and deliver artifacts to customer S3.
Support-1: Prepare an auditor-facing evidence bundle with signed manifest, checksums, and a copy of runbook describing signing process.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-13 17:15 UTC: Engineering deployed exporter v2 to eu-west behind feature flag. Deterministic checksum ordering and UTC canonicalization were included.

2026-03-13 19:40 UTC: SRE ran a one-off migration job that recreated the export for the customer's requested window and uploaded artifacts to their bucket. Delivered signed manifest that includes deletion_proof block for purged IDs and KMS signature reference.
2026-03-13 20:05 UTC: Support uploaded auditor evidence bundle to FinLeaf's secure file share and scheduled a verification call for 2026-03-14 09:00 CET.
Follow-ups: Document exporter v2 manifest schema in Confluence and add a Console toggle for 'include deletion proof' in exports.
